critical_code_review_comments: feature_calendar_recovery.py line 481-485 cleanly forwards V2 metadata (source, rationale, v2_priority, v2_intensity_target, v2_exposure_number) into the /calendar/range payload with `or None` guards so V1 rows leave these undefined — no risk of polluting legacy clients.

ClientCalendarPanel.tsx guards both rationale and priority pill rendering behind `card.workout.source === 'engine_v2'` — V1 rows can never accidentally show either UI. Priority pill styling is understated (border + textMuted) which matches the design brief of a soft badge.

workout/[id]/index.tsx uses the correct field names for the detail chips: `w.source === 'engine_v2'` gates on the top-level source flag and pulls from `w.v2_intensity_target` / `w.v2_exposure_number` which is what feature_v2_client_bridge.py:158-160 emits. No V1 leak surface.

The intensity chip on the home meta line uses `card.workout.intensity_target` (unprefixed, from /calendar/range) while the detail chip uses `w.v2_intensity_target` (prefixed, from /workouts/{id}). The two backend endpoints emit different keys — this is intentional and both were verified via curl, but it's a minor naming inconsistency worth flagging for future consolidation.
